findings.title: Promise 1 is not amended together: C1 Wave 0 leaves merge-train and duty 6 stale through Wave 1
findings.body: Spec A Part 6 and register R2 require promise 1's new shape in PHILOSOPHY, the covenant, showrunner duty 6, and merge-train.md to be amended together. The unreviewed C1-as-own-wave cut lands only PHILOSOPHY and the covenant in Wave 0 and forbids editing any other surface there. C2, which owns merge-train.md and showrunner duty 6, is Wave 2 after C1. Wave 1 (C9, C10, C12, C16, C17) therefore merges while the executable merge homes still contradict the founding texts C1 just shipped.
findings.suggestion: Sequence C2 immediately after C1 with no Wave 1 in between, or fold merge-train.md and showrunner duty 6 into C1 so the four promise-1 homes land in one change set.
findings.evidence: Spec A Part 6: "PHILOSOPHY promise 1, the covenant hard line, showrunner duty 6, and `merge-train.md`, all amended together." C1.md What: "No other surface is edited here." C1.md sequencing: "Wave 0, alone; the seam." coverage-map.md: "Wave 1, after C1 ... C9 ... C10, C12, C16, C17. Wave 2: C2 ..."

findings.title: C1 owns FR-B5 bullets 4 and 5 but states only the posture sentence
findings.body: The coverage map gives C1 exclusive ownership of Spec A FR-B5 bullet 4 (hard shell must stay tight) and bullet 5 (in-envelope variance is not defect evidence; a filing must show a shell breach or a stated bound exceeded). C1's What and DoD only land Change 5's posture sentence (bullet 1). C2's door text does not claim those bullets either, so they are owned on the map and absent from every child body.
findings.suggestion: Put FR-B5.4 in PHILOSOPHY beside the posture, and put FR-B5.5 in C1 or move ownership to C2's owner-decisions door with a DoD bullet a vet can grade (a filing that cites only in-envelope variance is declined).
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B5.4: "the hard shell must stay tight." FR-B5.5: "in-envelope variance is not defect evidence. A filing must show the shell was breached, or, only where the surface's declaration states a quantified bound ... that the bound was exceeded." C1.md What: "Change 5's posture (shrink the interface or tolerate before documenting the trap)." coverage-map.md owners: FR-B5.1 C1; FR-B5.4 C1; FR-B5.5 C1.

findings.title: FR-B6.2 plugin-root seam retirement has no child owner
findings.body: Spec A FR-B6.2 names the plugin-root seam and its lint as having met their delete-when condition, in the same record as harness_probe, and states that only the six orchestration pieces and the conditional heartbeat wait on the trial receipt. The coverage-map split of that bullet gives C9 the trial and C15 the retirements that wait on the receipt. R15 and C15 list the six pieces, heartbeat, harness_probe, re-arm, and the quota park; neither names plugin-root. The met-condition retirement is therefore unowned.
findings.suggestion: Give C15 an unconditional deletion of the plugin-root seam and its lint (it does not wait on C9), and name that piece in R15 and in the FR-B6.2 split text.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B6.2: "The plugin-root seam and its lint have met their delete-when condition (Codex aliases the variable); `harness_probe` retires or starts recording." Same bullet: "Only the six pieces and the conditional heartbeat wait on the receipt." coverage-map.md FR-B6.2 owner: "C9 owns the trial itself ... C15 owns the retirements that wait on that receipt." C15.md What lists the six pieces, heartbeat, harness_probe, re-arm, and the usage poller; not plugin-root.

findings.title: C6 DoD freezes the foundational set as only the covenant hard lines
findings.body: The keep-until-condition-fires restatement is otherwise aligned with Spec A FR-B3.12, but the new DoD bullet requires the foundational set to be exactly the covenant's hard lines. Spec A FR-B3.9–10 set that as the stamp default and then let the authority look add to the set. C6's later DoD bullet records which of the five authority surfaces the owner set to foundational, which cannot both be true of a set that must remain exactly the covenant lines.
findings.suggestion: Grade the stamp default as covenant hard lines, then grade the landing note for any authority-surface additions; do not assert the set is unchanged after the owner's look.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B3.9: "The foundational set at the stamp: the covenant's hard lines. ... The authority look below may add to the set." C6.md DoD: "the foundational set is exactly the covenant's hard lines." C6.md DoD: "the landing note records which the owner set to a condition and which to foundational."

findings.title: C12's six-case restatement drops case 6's certification-shape half
findings.body: Spec B FR-D8 case 6 requires a mixed hand-landed and dispatched panel to certify with per-seat provenance and the shape open item 7 rules (stamped as option (a): provenance-classed, so hand-landed seats do not silently equal full-panel-confirmed). The unreviewed six-case quote and its DoD stop at "certifies with the provenance field set per seat." A fixture that certifies a mixed panel as full-panel-confirmed would pass C12 and fail the spec.
findings.suggestion: Restore the spec's case-6 expected answer: mixed panel certifies with per-seat provenance and the FR-D2 (a) shape (audited-chain, not full-panel-confirmed).
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8: "a panel mixing hand-landed and dispatched seats (certifies with the provenance field set per seat and the shape open item 7 rules)." Stamp item 7: "The receipt writer labels each seat's provenance in its own field, separate from the coverage shape." C12.md What case (6): "a panel mixing hand-landed and dispatched seats certifies with the provenance field set per seat." C12.md DoD: "mixed panel certifies with per-seat provenance."

findings.title: R8 dropped-MOVE echo-nothing collides with the FR-M7 family line still saying move-with-echo
findings.body: Unreviewed R8 says MOVE rows that are dropped read nothing, resolve no caller input, and echo nothing, matching Spec B FR-M1. The coverage map's FR-M7.3 split and C10's family sentence still tell the builder that self-vouching rows other than scrub and containment "move with echo," which is Spec B FR-M7.3's including-drop wording. C10's What also contains both sentences. A builder following the family line will echo dropped self-vouching rows and violate R8. C10's new DoD lets a dropped row pass if it "reads nothing," with no echo-nothing check.
findings.suggestion: Change the FR-M7.3 split text and C10's family sentence to: remainder MOVE rows that default or accept more shapes echo; dropped remainder rows echo nothing. Add echo-nothing to the C10 DoD dropped leg.
findings.evidence: R8: "the MOVE rows that are dropped read nothing, resolve no caller input, and echo nothing." Spec B FR-M1: "a dropped row reads nothing, so its `resolves-caller-input` column is no by construction." coverage-map.md FR-M7.3: "scrub and containment keep; the rest move with echo." C10.md What: "dropped MOVE rows reading nothing and echoing nothing" and, later, "the rest move with echo." C10.md DoD: "dropped and reads nothing."

findings.title: C17's declared-dependencies DoD grades the wrong four surfaces
findings.body: Spec A FR-E1's declared dependencies are surfaces the rules read but do not create: (i) a launch ledger, (ii) a standing-proposals collector with a pinned registry surface, (iii) a consumer path for FR-B3 back-fill, (iv) the detector-shaped-test boundary. C17's What substitutes a durable owner-visible collector, a pinned registry surface, the kind labels, and a lane field on vet receipts. Kind labels are created at calibration, so they cannot be a declared dependency. The unreviewed DoD bullet requires a calibration-time check of "the four declared dependencies" as the body names them, so a PR can pass while the spec's four go unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Name Spec A FR-E1's four dependencies in the What and DoD; keep kind-label creation as a separate calibration act, not as dependency (iii) or (iv).
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-E1: "four surfaces the rules above read but do not create" listing launch ledger; standing-proposals collector with pinned registry; FR-B3 consumer path; detector-shaped-test boundary. C17.md What: "the four declared dependencies ... (a durable owner-visible collector, a pinned registry surface, the kind labels, and a lane field on vet receipts)." C17.md DoD: "Each of the four declared dependencies has a recorded calibration-time check, and calibration on a repo without the two kind labels creates them."

findings.title: C17 fail-direction DoD checks the wrong shipped defaults and omits the P2 carve-out
findings.body: Spec A FR-E1's shipped defaults are the dial, N's derivation, the three condition windows, guardian staleness, and keep-or-retire reporting (no). C17's What instead lists dial, condition windows, guardian thresholds, the material line, and the P0 definition. The new DoD bullet says "the only defaults present are the five the spec permits" while the body lists a different five, so a vet grading from the PR and body will accept the wrong set. The same fail-direction rule also inactivates the P2-files-free carve-out with no stamped ladder; the DoD only records a P0/P1 refusal.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the spec's five shipped defaults in the DoD table, and add a recorded case that a no-ladder project cannot use the P2 carve-out.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-E1 fail direction: "The shipped defaults are the dial (20–30%), N's derivation from it, the three condition windows, the guardian staleness thresholds, and keep-or-retire reporting (no)." Same bullet: "no P0 or P1 can be claimed and the P2-files-free carve-out is inactive." C17.md What: "plugin default where the spec gives one (the dial's range, the condition windows, the guardian thresholds, the material line, the P0 definition)." C17.md DoD: "the only defaults present are the five the spec permits" and "cannot claim a P0 or P1 ... shown by a recorded refusal."

findings.title: C14 Astra DoD does not grade the stamped pass or the three-miss proposal
findings.body: Spec B FR-S9 and R14 allow Astra to take reviewer-deep only after a live security-lens dispatch names a planted fail-open by file, line, and severity; three misses put the question to the owner. C14's new DoD treats any annex "pass" as sufficient and, on a miss, only checks that Sol is unchanged and a receipt discloses pending registration. A pass that is a refusal, an unrelated finding, or a plant named without line and severity would still satisfy the DoD.
findings.suggestion: Require the recorded pass to quote file, line, and severity from that dispatch's own result, and require a three-miss annex row to show the owner proposal.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-S9: "returns a finding that names the plant by location (the `file`, `line`, and `severity` standard ...) not a refusal and not an unrelated finding. ... Three misses propose to the owner whether the question stays open." C14.md DoD: "The Astra probe attempts are recorded in the annex; if the pass is recorded, the registry shows Astra at reviewer-deep at effort high ... if not, Sol is unchanged and a receipt ... carries the pending-registration disclosure."

findings.title: C13's out-of-scope certify DoD does not read the revisit trigger or class-closure
findings.body: C13's What promises the three dispositions are recorded with revisit-trigger and class-closure lines. Spec B FR-D8 says an out-of-scope disposition is not a disposition without those two lines, and the writer refuses a follow-up with no trigger. The new DoD only requires a Minor finding dispositioned out of scope with a follow-up to certify. A follow-up whose trigger is "documented", or that omits class closure, would pass the DoD and fail the spec.
findings.suggestion: In the same dry run, require the follow-up item to show a condition/date/milestone trigger (not "documented") and a class-closure line, and show that a missing trigger does not certify.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8: "an out-of-scope disposition carries two things or it is not a disposition. First, a revisit trigger ... never \"documented\"; the receipt writer refuses a follow-up item with no trigger line. Second, class closure ..." C13.md What: "the three dispositions recorded in the loop record with the revisit trigger and class-closure lines." C13.md DoD: "A fixture review with one Minor finding dispositioned out of scope with a follow-up certifies on the round it is dispositioned."

findings.title: C11 probe DoD omits the substitute-or-park step the child promises
findings.body: C11's What includes the conformance probe's substitute-or-park step. Spec B FR-S5 and R10 require that when the owner launches without a failed engine that supplied a lane's second family, the preflight names the substitute family or parks those full lanes. The new DoD only records a loud failure naming the engine and what failed. A probe that fails loudly and then launches the condemned full lanes would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Add a recorded broken-engine preflight that shows either the named substitute family or the parked full lanes beside the owner's choice.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-S5: "When the owner launches without the engine and it supplied a lane's second family, the preflight names the substitute family under the seat map's existing substitution rule or parks that wave's full lanes; it never launches a lane the second-family check already condemns." C11.md What: "its failure loud and its result recorded in the preflight record, with the substitute-or-park step." C11.md DoD: "a deliberately broken engine configuration produces a loud failure naming the engine and what failed, recorded in a preflight record shown in the PR body."
